title: Turning Multiple Myeloma From a 3-Year Sentence Into Deep Remission: 20S Proteasome Traps to CD38 & BCMA/GPRC5D Bispecifics — 20S Proteasome Traps (Bortezomib 5LF3, Carfilzomib 4R67), CD38 (Daratumumab 7DHA, PERSEUS), BCMA–APRIL (1XU2), Cilta-cel (CARTITUDE-4), Teclistamab & Talquetamab

teenKit.tldr: Multiple myeloma turns plasma cells into redline-overheating antibody factories, but scientists learned to weaponize that exact overcapacity using atomic-scale molecular traps.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Transforming a fatal 3-year death sentence into deep, long-term remission shows how mapping biology down to individual atoms can completely conquer a once-hopeless cancer.
keyTakeaways: Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells that pumps out massive amounts of proteins, making it run at a catastrophic biological overcapacity.
Medicines like bortezomib and carfilzomib act as microscopic traps that jam the cell's waste-disposal system, forcing the overactive factory to self-destruct from its own toxic garbage.
Modern therapies combine these molecular traps with precision immunotherapies like bispecific antibodies and CAR-T cells to hunt down and destroy cancer cells with incredible accuracy.

vocab.meaning: A cancer of bone marrow plasma cells that relentlessly mass-produces abnormal proteins until the cell chokes on its own output.
The cellular shredder or recycling plant that chops up old or damaged proteins to keep the cell running smoothly.
A lab-engineered dual-target protein that acts like molecular Velcro, gluing a killer T-cell directly to a cancer cell to destroy it.
A state where cancer signs and symptoms significantly decrease or completely disappear from the body.

quiz.question: Why is a multiple myeloma cell's intense protein production considered its fatal flaw?
options: It makes the cells visible to standard X-rays
It forces the cell to run at a redlined overcapacity that makes it vulnerable to cellular waste overload
It causes the blood to turn completely acidic
It stops the patient from producing normal red blood cells
quiz.explanation: Because the cell mass-produces proteins at a frantic pace, blocking its recycling shredder causes toxic trash to pile up instantly, triggering self-destruction.

quiz.question: What is the primary job of proteasome inhibitors like bortezomib and carfilzomib?
options: To jam the cell's waste-disposal system so toxic proteins accumulate
To mutate the patient's DNA into a healthy sequence
To boost the heart rate to fight off tumors
To dissolve the bone marrow completely
quiz.explanation: These drugs bind to the proteasome's active sites, shutting down the cellular shredder and causing fatal protein traffic jams inside the cancer cell.

quiz.question: How do modern precision therapies like bispecific antibodies help treat this cancer?
options: By tricking the immune system into eating the patient's bones
By physically bridging the patient's own killer T-cells directly to proteins on the surface of the cancer cells
By replacing the bone marrow with synthetic gel
By turning off the patient's nervous system temporarily
quiz.explanation: Bispecific antibodies act as dual-ended clamps that grab a T-cell with one hand and a myeloma cell marker with the other, forcing the immune system to execute the cancer.
